bounds.domain: One direct benchmark child, two observed output changes, four successful progress receipts, one monitor failure and up to two existing termination-helper calls.
bounds.scope: The monitor retains direct-child ownership through normal exit, cancellation, deadline and observation or progress-write failure. A successful cleanup boundary reaps the direct child. A refused cleanup reports both errors and preserves an explicit unconfirmed outcome. Descendant process groups, provider work, result publication, arbitrary filesystem behavior and Windows adapter conformance remain outside the projection.

assumptions: Weak fairness of advance means pending termination/wait and progress-write operations eventually settle with success or error. A refused cleanup may retain a live child and cannot report confirmed resource release.
Healthy monitoring does not require eventual benchmark exit. Deadline detection, output timing and signal grace are abstract boundaries, with no elapsed-time termination guarantee.
No fairness is assumed. A wait or receipt write may remain pending forever after shutdown is requested.
